draft.headline: Tech selloff drags Nasdaq down 3.4%, then a sharp late bounce
draft.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 3.44% to 28,545 as tech sold off, then jumped 0.93% in the last measured hour. The supplied headlines do not clearly explain either move.
draft.what_it_means: The supplied headlines point at tech-specific selling. One says US tech stocks saw sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn. Another describes tech getting crushed while defensive stocks shine. Reddit plunged 30% after a weak outlook, and a $6.3 billion crypto exchange hack added a risk-off tone. None of these is a confirmed cause of a 3.4% index drop, and nothing supplied explains the late bounce. Treat the reason as unclear.
draft.market_reaction: NQ ended the day 3.44% lower at 28,545, below yesterday's low and last week's low. Its 942-point range was 196% of a typical day. In the last hour it rose 0.93% while the VIX fear gauge dropped 13.02%. S&P 500 futures fell 1.81% on the day, gold lost 3.49% and oil gained 1.12%.
draft.rates_read: Yields fell on the day: the 10-year dropped 6.8bp to 4.921% and the 2-year 7.1bp to 4.585%. Lower yields usually help Nasdaq stocks, because future profits are worth more today, yet NQ still fell hard. So yields do not explain the drop. In the last hour, yields barely moved while NQ bounced.

draft.learn: VXN is the Nasdaq's 'fear gauge': it shows how much price swings options traders expect over the next year, as a yearly rate. At 29.40 it sits 9.88 points above the VIX, meaning options markets expect more turbulence in tech than in the wider market.
